text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Leading members of the ruling Social Democratic party, including house speaker Erling Olsen are to campaign for a lifting of Denmark's opt-outs on the Maastricht Treaty. In 1993 Danes voted for the treaty on condition that Denmark stayed out of the single European currency, joint defence, EU citizenship and legal and police cooperation.

--Novo Nordisk is to cut the price of its insulin sold in phials by about 20 percent in Denmark, to around the same price as competitor Eli Lilly. Some 35,000 Danish insulin users are expected to benefit from the price war.

--At a conference in parliament, prime minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen said he would first formally announce whether or not Denmark would next year hold a referendum on Europe after the EU Amsterdam summit next week. He said expansion to embrace new eastern European members was EU's most important next move and was strongly supported by his government.

--Leading Danish mortgage credit institution Nykredit is deeply split on staying in the sales and marketing alliance with third biggest bank BG Bank and leading insurer Topdanmark. At a board meeting on Thursday Nykredit is to decide whether to strengthen its alliance with the bank-insurance grouping or quit it, with analysts expecting the cooperation pact to continue.

--In the present atmosphere of uncertainty about EMU, Danish prime minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen echoes economic wisemen's advice for Denmark to stay out of Europe's single currency until it has proved to be strong and membership beneficial.
